classification.difficultyReason: Identify the shorter side in a practical kite problem, apply Pythagoras’ theorem and convert the height to centimetres before rounding.

inlines.text: A kite is flying with 42 m of string which is anchored to the ground.
The horizontal distance from where the string is anchored is 27 m.
Find the height of the kite above the ground to the nearest centimetre.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 diagram beneath the prompt, on the left
spec.description: A string rises from a ground anchor at the lower left to an outlined kite at the upper right. The height is a dashed vertical line with a right-angle marker at the ground.
spec.mathematics: The string is the 42 m hypotenuse; the horizontal leg is 27 m and the vertical leg is x. The kite and trailing tail identify the upper endpoint.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given lengths and unknown x are visible; no calculated height is shown.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}a^2+b^2&=h^2\\x^2+27^2&=42^2\\x^2&=42^2-27^2\\x^2&=1035\\x&=\sqrt{1035}\text{ m}\\x&=100\sqrt{1035}\text{ cm}\\x&\approx3217\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The kite is 3217 cm above the ground, to the nearest centimetre.
